title: Fix Bun prebuild file name in Node binding
description:
Fixes #205.

The Bun branch of `bindings/node/index.js` required `tree-sitter-r.node`. prebuildify names the artifact after `name` in `package.json` with `/` replaced by `+`, and the package is scoped, so the tarball ships `@davisvaughan+tree-sitter-r.node`. The two never matched, so `require()` threw at load time for every Bun user, on every platform.

Node was never affected — `node-gyp-build` scans the prebuilds directory instead of constructing the name — which is why this went unnoticed.

One line, plus a comment tying the string to `package.json` so the two stay linked if the package is ever renamed or unscoped.

## Verified

Clean install of the published 1.3.0, then the same install with this branch's `index.js` dropped in:

```console
$ bun add @davisvaughan/tree-sitter-r

# published 1.3.0
$ bun -e "require('@davisvaughan/tree-sitter-r'); console.log('OK')"
error: Cannot find module '../../prebuilds/win32-x64/tree-sitter-r.node' from
'…/node_modules/@davisvaughan/tree-sitter-r/bindings/node/index.js'

# with this change
$ bun -e "const R = require('@davisvaughan/tree-sitter-r'); console.log('OK', typeof R)"
OK object

# Node, unchanged
$ node -e "const R = require('@davisvaughan/tree-sitter-r'); console.log('OK', typeof R)"
OK object
```

Bun 1.4.0, Node v24.16.0, Windows x64. I only have Windows to hand, but the file name is derived from the package name rather than the platform, so the other prebuild directories carry the same `@davisvaughan+` prefix and should behave identically.

Happy to adjust the CHANGELOG wording, or drop that bullet entirely if you would rather write it at release time.

title: fix: Exclude Trailing `\r` from Comment Nodes on CRLF-Formatted Files
description:
Currently, when parsing files with CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings, comment nodes incorrectly include the trailing `\r` character.

This PR updates the grammar to exclude `\r` from the comment node content, aligning the behavior with other grammars such as [tree-sitter-javascript](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-javascript/blob/6fbef40512dcd9f0a61ce03a4c9ae7597b36ab5c/grammar.js#L974).

#### Example Input

```text
# comment
```

### Output of `tree-sitter parse` 

#### Before this PR

```lisp
(program [0, 0] - [1, 0]
  (comment [0, 0] - [0, 10]))
```

#### Using this PR

```lisp
(program [0, 0] - [1, 0]
  (comment [0, 0] - [0, 9]))
```

---

* Also fixes formatting of `grammar.js` in line 74 and 208/209.

title: Split raw strings into open/content/close
description:
Closes #195 

Removes a TODO, fixes a bug, and improves uniformity by splitting raw strings into their open / content / close parts, giving us a single uniform `string` node structure regardless of the type of R string that it is!

Before

(Note the lack of a breakdown for `_raw_string_literal`, you can't access its inner information. And the `"open"` fields previously mapped to `"` or `'` directly, but will now map to a more general `string_open` node type.)

```js
    string: $ => choice(
      $._raw_string_literal, // <- came from external scanner
      $._single_quoted_string,
      $._double_quoted_string
    ),

    _single_quoted_string: $ => seq(
      field("open", '\''),
      optional(field("content", alias($._single_quoted_string_content, $.string_content))),
      field("close", '\'')
    ),

    _double_quoted_string: $ => seq(
      field("open", '"'),
      optional(field("content", alias($._double_quoted_string_content, $.string_content))),
      field("close", '"')
    ),
```

After

```js
    string: $ => choice(
      $._raw_string,
      $._single_quoted_string,
      $._double_quoted_string
    ),

    _raw_string: $ => seq(
      field("open", alias($._raw_string_open, $.string_open)),
      optional(field("content", alias($._raw_string_content, $.string_content))),
      field("close", alias($._raw_string_close, $.string_close))
    ),

    _single_quoted_string: $ => seq(
      field("open", alias('\'', $.string_open)),
      optional(field("content", alias($._single_quoted_string_content, $.string_content))),
      field("close", alias('\'', $.string_close))
    ),

    _double_quoted_string: $ => seq(
      field("open", alias('"', $.string_open)),
      optional(field("content", alias($._double_quoted_string_content, $.string_content))),
      field("close", alias('"', $.string_close))
    ),
```

All `string` variants now share the same _field names_ and _child node structure_, which should be a very nice move towards uniformity. All `string`s now have:

- An `'open'` field containing a `string_open` node (`'`, `"`, or a raw string opening sequence).
- An optional `'content'` field containing a `string_content` node.
- A `'close'` field containing a `string_close` node (`'`, `"`, or a raw string closing sequence).

---

Notes to self:

Much more involved than I originally thought due to the need to store some `RawStringState` in the buffer between `scan()`s. Required some refactoring of the `scopes` array details to make storing arbitrary things in the `buffer` more composable.

One notable thing I learned is that `TREE_SITTER_SERIALIZATION_BUFFER_SIZE` isn't optional. When your `serialize()` hook is called, the `char* buffer` you can serialize into is exactly `TREE_SITTER_SERIALIZATION_BUFFER_SIZE`. So writing more than this is an OOB error. Similarly, reading more than this in your `deserialize()` hook is also not allowed.

I considered whether `.string` should be split from `.raw_string`, but I think keeping them together makes the most sense. In the R grammar, both strings and raw strings are given the token `STR_CONST` and can be used interchangeably in the grammar and are indistinguishable from one another.
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/00a0f951b09455cbe4d0567a13f9a428d65127fb/src/main/gram.y#L3191
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/00a0f951b09455cbe4d0567a13f9a428d65127fb/src/main/gram.y#L3331

Claude gave two quite good reviews that helped catch a lot of edge cases, uploaded here for future reference
[review.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28274723/review.md)
[review2.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28274724/review2.md)

title: Don't consume `else` if it is part of a larger `identifier`
description:
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/200

We can't directly emulate the JS side `XID_Continue` or R's `iswalnum()` in UTF-8 locale, so this is a best effort approach, but I think it should work pretty well in all but the most pathological cases. And even in those pathological cases, R would generate a syntax error on something that we'd parse. So the important thing is that R isn't parsing something that we reject.

title: Reject `.[digit]` as an `identifier`
description:
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/190

Turns out that both `.1L` and `.1i` were being incorrectly parsed as `identifier`

R itself actually rejects `.[digit]` as an identifier, presumably for this exact reason, because it is ambiguous with integer literals and complex literals and floats in general.

So the most correct solution is to also forbid `.[digit]` in the grammar too, making `identifier` more correct, and fixing the `.1L` and `.1i` cases all in one swoop

title: Simplify identifier without changing the grammar
description:
Closes #176 

I toyed with merging `$.dots` and `$.dot_dot_i` into `$.identifier`, there were two options:

- Just remove `$.dots` and `$.dot_dot_i` altogether and let `$.identifier` handle them both. This is theoretically pleasing because the `gram.y` doesn't treat `...` and `..i` specially, but I decided against it because people do give `dots` and `dot_dot_i` special highlighting (i.e. neovim). Doing this is supported by the fact that `?Reserved` in R mentions that these are both _reserved words_, and if you look at the set of reserved words there, we provide nodes for all other ones, so it is reasonable to have these too.

- Nest `$.dots` and `$.dot_dot_i` under `$.identifier`. This would also be somewhat nice, as an indication that they are just "special" identifiers. But this is fairly disruptive because it would be a breaking change. It is also kind of annoying because:
    - We use `identifier` as the `word` right now, which must be a simple token, so we'd have to change that
    - We'd probably structure `$.identifier` as a `choice($.dots, $.dot_dot_i, $._normal_identifier)`, since that is the least disruptive approach, as it doesn't change the tree structure for most identifiers. But that leaves us with a terminal node that is also hidden (`_normal_identifier`), making `ts_node_is_missing()` useless https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/blob/29c816328a086ef056799e3924ef6e09e6a9a8cb/grammar.js#L562-L567

So instead I've kept `$.dots` and `$.dot_dot_i` and introduced a new _inline_ `$._identifier` wrapper that is a `choice()` around all 3 of these, and I use that everywhere as our identifier. The _inline_ bit seems critical to ensure that things like `prec()` get applied to the inlined nodes and not the wrapping hidden node (I've left a comment about this). 

This is nice because it simplifies our naming scheme, while keeping the grammar the same.

title: Document our rationale for treating `]]` as a single literal token
description:
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/78

I've decided that the usefulness of treating `]]` as a single literal token...
- Can treat call, subset, subset2 nodes exactly the same
- Literal tokens in the grammar for all of `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `[[`, and `]]`
- Simplicity of the grammar

...outweighs the benefits of precisely supporting the R grammar here:
- Maybe 1 in a million R scripts won't parse because of this. I have never seen anyone put space between the `]]`.

title: Improve on support for `...` and `..i` in odd places
description:
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/148

This is motivated by needing support for `x$...`, which is the most common case of this weirdness. But I've managed to tighten up quite a few of these extremely obscure cases while making things consistent. All of these are valid R code:

- `x$...` and `x@...`
- `x$..1` and `x@..1`
- `foo::...` and `...::foo` (and `:::` versions)
- `foo::..i` and `..i:::foo` (and `:::` versions)
- `for (... in 1:2) print(get("..."))`
- `for (..1 in 1:2) print(get("..1"))`
- `function(..1) get("..1")`
- `function(..1 = 2) get("..1")`
- `fn(..1 = 2)`
- `fn(... = 2)`

I went with the approach we talked about of keeping `$.identifier`, `$.dots`, and `$.dot_dot_i` as separate nodes (because they are useful to downstream consumers), and making a union type of `$._identifier_or_dots_or_dot_dot_i` that gets used internally.

The commits are technically backwards. I wrote the impl but didn't commit it until I committed all the updated tests first, just to make sure it was correct. Probably easiest to read each commit individually.

title: Update to tree-sitter 0.23
description:
Tree-sitter released version 0.23 recently. This contains a breaking, but ultimately very good change to how parser bindings work (https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/pull/3069). The TLDR of that change is that parsers do not depend on tree-sitter anymore, but instead on a shard (and supposedly very stable) tree-sitter-language crate. As a result, clients are free to chose their tree-sitter version as the parser ABI is supported. Library and parser versions are less tighly coupled, and it should no longer be necessary to move all the parsers to the next tree-sitter version in lock-step to be able to upgrade the library.

Most of the changes in this PR are from running tree-sitter generate. I'll add comments on other changes I did to explain why I thought they are necessary, or where I'm not sure I did it correctly.

title: Inline `_identifier` and `_quoted_identifier`
description:
Requires https://github.com/DavisVaughan/r-tree-sitter/pull/7 for its updated print method used in snapshot tests

https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/issues/3332 prevents us from being able to use `ts_node_is_missing()` in many places because our `identifier` node has internal "hidden" rules. While we wait for this to be fixed, we can workaround this by inlining those hidden rules, being careful about the fact that we still need a "terminal" rule that can be used for `word`.

I've changed from `_identifier` to `identifier` for use in `word`, but I don't think included quoted identifiers is going to make much of a difference for what `word` is used for (distinguishing keywords like `if` and `function` from identifiers)

title: Allow `_` as the leading character of an `identifier`
description:
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/71

So `_foo` is now parsed as a single identifier, even if it is invalid R code. This gives downstream consumers an opportunity to at least do a follow up check that the `identifier` is valid R code using their own means (some regex check probably).

Previously `_foo` was being parsed as two identifiers: `_` and `foo`. This was because we allowed a single `token("_")` to represent the pipe placeholder. If we removed that, then we could instead error on `_foo` as invalid syntax. But then to support `_` we'd have to add in very specific rules around `|>` to define the scopes where a long `_` pipe placeholder is allowed, and that doesn't seem worth it, even if it is technically probably more correct (I do think `main` tries something like this).

title: Document our official state on keywords
description:
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/98
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/84

Must be a `?Reserved` word specially handled by R's parser. ~This means we are removing `return` as a keyword, and downstream consumers can highlight this specially if they want.~ We decided to keep `return` as the _one_ exception to this rule, because it is _so_ special.

This generally uses the same rationale as `binary_operator`, where rather than adding special handling for `|>` and other binary operators in their own nodes, we instead stop the grammar at semantic behavior and lump them all together as `binary_operator`.

title: feat: create and expose `string_content` node for easier captures
description:
This PR creates a sub node to `string` called `string_content`. The reasoning is, that it makes it easier to capture the content with a tree-sitter query.

Potential use case: having a function that takes in a SQL statement as a string to query a data base. This could be captured and highlighted as well.

The Python parser implemented this as well, see [here](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python/blob/7c8930b6388b5590ebef248853f144185a9eda1d/grammar.js#L952)

Note: I have ran `tree-sitter test -u` to update the test cases. There were not `ERROR` or `MISSING`. This fixed also the formatting in the test files.

title: Add `escape_sequence` and `string_content` nodes
description:
Part of https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/98
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/pull/52

Adds `escape_sequence` back in, which was part of `main` but was removed in `next`. I think being able to highlight an escape sequence is pretty neat.

Also adds a `string_content` node, which many other grammars have. This gives you just the content of the string, dropping the `"` and the `'` pair surrounding it. Useful when marshaling the string contents into a Rust or C string, for example. This is _not_ yet implemented for raw strings, as I think it will take a little fiddling and should be left as another PR.

I started with the definition of `escape_sequence` on `main` and then refined it based on many many examples which have all become tests (the R package snapshot tests are way more informative here).

The most useful file is actually `strings.md` where you can see the text and the nodes one after the other.

title: Add `tags.scm` support
description:
Closes https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/issues/80

Based on these examples
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python/blob/master/queries/tags.scm
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-javascript/blob/master/queries/tags.scm
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-rust/blob/master/queries/tags.scm

And the Category/Tag table in this section
https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/code-navigation-systems#examples

I used these
- `@definition.function`
- `@reference.call`

I don't _think_ we want any for class, interface, method, module, or implementation. The module one seems interesting, as it is somewhat related to package names, i.e. `dplyr::` or `library(dplyr)`, but I don't think it maps to anything, i.e. `definition.module` would be the creation of the "dplyr module", which is like `namespace dplyr {` in C++, but no equivalent in R, and there doesn't seem to be a `reference.module` oddly.

There also seems to be an undocumented one for constants but I don't think that works for us either
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python/blob/a22761025cdac6c314b7e3aa48fb44fa9e594d6a/queries/tags.scm#L1

Let me know if you can think of something I'm missing!

title: R package
description:
Full dump of the first pass at the treesitterr package (could be called treesitter.r if we wanted, might be smart).

- One tweak to `src/scanner.c` right now, using `"tree_sitter/parser.h"` rather than `<tree_sitter/parser.h>`, just so it will compile (couldn't "find" it otherwise)
- Otherwise all the changes are localized to `bindings/r`

This adds the R package for the _R grammar_ itself. These are not bindings to tree-sitter in general. That's elsewhere (https://github.com/DavisVaughan/r-tree-sitter). The grammar is exposed through a single function `language()`, which is then consumed by the treesitter package (it also provides the print method for the language class).

## Tests

I have completely ported the tree sitter tests over to R snapshot tests, and they are now way easier to read and work with IMO. You can also test more extensive things, including error cases. You write tests in, say, `references/calls.R` and they show up as snapshot tests in `_snaps/calls.md`. Each section divided by `# -----` gets its own `test_that()` block, and then each top level expression within that block is printed out separately of the others, making it very easy to see the s-expr that goes with a particular line of text.
https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/blob/7b47a21c9a01c106098fe53fb48b9b801eb3d6c2/bindings/r/tests/testthat/_snaps/calls.md
https://github.com/r-lib/tree-sitter-r/blob/7b47a21c9a01c106098fe53fb48b9b801eb3d6c2/bindings/r/tests/testthat/references/calls.R

In the long term, if these bindings are intended to be fully auto generated, then we might want to have `treesitter.r.tests` as an R package that never makes it to CRAN, but imports both `treesitter.r` and `treesitter` and is actually where all the tests live. We would run its tests every time a PR is sent to r-tree-sitter, and that would be its sole purpose.

## parser.c

Currently, the R package bundles a second copy of `parser.c` in `bindings/r/src/parser.c` that is updated through a call to `update()`, an internal helper. I do not currently know of a better way to do this, but this is kind of annoying

title: Be more WASM compatible
description:
Closes #85 

As mentioned in #85, unfortunately we do a few things that aren't WASM compatible, preventing `tree-sitter build-wasm` from working right. Using `exit()` and `vprintf()` are also _bad things_ from the point of view of being included in an R package.

I've worked around the following issues:
- Home grown compilation flag `TREE_SITTER_R_DEBUG` for debugging. This allows us to put usage of `vprintf()` behind a compilation flag that is generally off, making both WASM and R check happy. It also removes our usage of `getenv()`, which isn't supported by WASM either. It seems simpler for us to do this rather than trying to keep using `getenv("TREE_SITTER_DEBUG")`.

- Swap `isspace()` for `iswspace()`. It turns out that tree-sitter supports `iswspace()` in their WASM builds, but not `isspace()`. I don't know why that is, but its easy enough for us to switch back. Presumably that is why we were using this in the first place before I moved us to `isspace()`? https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/lib/src/wasm/stdlib-symbols.txt

- Fixed up one `()` -> `(void)` signature on our end

- Avoid calling `exit()` entirely, by instead doing a debug log and returning a `NULL` pointer back, which we check for in the other 4 tree-sitter hooks (scan, serialize, deserialize, destroy) before proceeding. A shame we have to care about this at all, but what can you do 🤷 .

As of this PR, `tree-sitter build-wasm` works again!

title: Rename nodes to avoid usage of special characters
description:
This PR renames nodes in the grammar which used special characters (operators, brackets, ...). These nodes would give errors when the parse was loaded with the Node.js bindings for tree-sitter. (The bindings try to create a class with the node name, but since special characters are not allowed, it fails with a `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '?'`). 

I've used the [R source code](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/main/gram.y) and [language reference](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-lang.html) to pick names. I am not very familiar with R, so better names are probably possible. Feel free to suggest alternatives!

I confirm that with these new names, the Node.js bindings work, so this PR fixes #62.

title: Replace `.` with `(.|\n)` to truly allow ANY character after a backslash
description:
@kevinushey my proposed alternative of `/'((?:\\')|[^'])*'/` actually wasn't quite right, because it allowed `'\'` and thought that was a string, when really that's an unclosed single quote due to the escaped `\'`.

So I think the original regex was mostly right, we just need to also account for `\n` since the handling of `.` is explicitly written as "every character except `\n`" in the tree sitter regex handler:
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/d92a7a969099a0a2db61a0ba5e6275e71e09c637/cli/src/generate/prepare_grammar/expand_tokens.rs#L249-L251

I'm copying the bash implementation here with `(.|\n)`
https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-bash/blob/975bc70ad95dbbf2733872bc2e0a059c055db983/grammar.js#L837

It seems like you would typically use a `/s` (DOTALL) flag, or something like `[^]`, to accomplish this, but neither of those work in the tree sitter regex implementation.

title: Proporsal: support default_parameter and default_argument
description:
### Problem

Currently the parser does not have a rule for default arguments and parameters. This creates a somewhat cluttered tree which can make writing queries difficult.

Example:

```r
rnorm(1, 10)
rnorm(1, mean = 10)
```

```
call [0, 0] - [0, 12]
  function: identifier [0, 0] - [0, 5]
  arguments: arguments [0, 6] - [0, 11]
    value: float [0, 6] - [0, 7]
    value: float [0, 9] - [0, 11]
call [1, 0] - [1, 19]
  function: identifier [1, 0] - [1, 5]
  arguments: arguments [1, 6] - [1, 18]
    value: float [1, 6] - [1, 7]
    name: identifier [1, 9] - [1, 13]
    value: float [1, 16] - [1, 18]
```

## Solution

Add two rules:

1. `default_paramater` (used in function definition)
2. `default_argument` (used in call function)


With new rule `default_argument`:

```
(call [0, 0] - [0, 12]
    function: (identifier [0, 0] - [0, 5])
    arguments: (arguments [0, 6] - [0, 11]
      (float [0, 6] - [0, 7])
      (float [0, 9] - [0, 11])))
  (call [1, 0] - [1, 19]
    function: (identifier [1, 0] - [1, 5])
    arguments: (arguments [1, 6] - [1, 18]
      (float [1, 6] - [1, 7])
      (default_argument [1, 9] - [1, 18]
        name: (identifier [1, 9] - [1, 13])
        value: (float [1, 16] - [1, 18]))))
```

description:
This PR add new hightlights.

3. `::` and `:::` as `@operator`
4. dollar `$` as `@operator`

9. `nan`, `na` and `null` as `@type.builtin`

title: Use version range for `tree-sitter` dependency
description:
Using this range avoids the Rust compiler error,

```
expected struct `tree_sitter::Language`, found a different struct `tree_sitter::Language`
perhaps two different versions of crate `tree_sitter` are being used?
```

which is encountered when using this crate along side `tree-sitter-python`, `tree-sitter-javascript` and `tree-sitter-typescript`. The range is consistent with the range used in those crates e.g. https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python/blob/master/Cargo.toml).

title: Add a Cargo.toml so that this grammar can be used as a Rust crate
description:
This simplifies usage a great deal when integrating into a Rust project. The `Cargo.toml` is based heavily on https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python/blob/master/Cargo.toml.

Ideally this would be published on crates.io along side `tree-sitter-python`, `tree-sitter-javascript` etc. I'd be happy to assist with that if so desired.

title: Add new highlight groups
description:
This PR adds new highlight groups. I tried following existing practice in other languages. In particular, group `@function` seems to be used for both function calls and function definition. I also decided to use `@function.method` for namespace calls, which might be questionable as it can have not only functions, but seems to be appropriate.

I added those groups which I could think of. If there are some highlighting groups which you wanted to created but never got time, please let me know.

title: Add fields to 'unary' and 'binary' rules.
description:
This PR addresses small inconsistency between tree-sitter grammars for R and other languages. It relates to how unary and binary operations are parsed.

Currently only special operator is parsed as [named node](https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/using-parsers#named-vs-anonymous-nodes). This seems to eliminate the possibility of making queries which depend on operator: for example, I couldn't find a way to make a query for binary formula (`a ~ b`).

This PR is basically an adaptation from other languages (like [Python](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python/blob/3196e288650992bca2399dda15ac703c342a22bb/grammar.js#L590), [Rust](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-rust/blob/2beedf23bedbd7b02b416518693e8eed3944d4a0/grammar.js#L939), [JavaScript](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-javascript/blob/3d906f36a62e4cf165f5baa9626db905584d9752/grammar.js#L736)). It makes parts of parsed binary and unary operations to be fields. This enables queries for formula to be `(binary operator: "~") @formula`.

Couple of questions:

- In most languages rules for unary and binary operators are not called simply 'unary' and 'binary'. What do you think about renaming them for more consistency (although there isn't much to begin with)? Some options: 'binary_expression' (seems to be most common), 'binary_operator', 'binary_operation'.
- Names for parts of binary operator seem to be consistent across languages: 'left', 'operator', 'right'. For unary operator not so much. What are your thoughts on names chosen in this PR ('operator', 'operand')? They were chosen from Ruby which also has 'binary' and 'unary' names. Other common choice is 'operator', 'argument'.

If these changes are OK, I'll update tests and other necessary files.

title: Add a basic gitignore file (based on other tree-sitter-* projects)
description:
Hello, I'm Martin from r2c, working on [semgrep](https://semgrep.dev). 

This PR adds a `.gitignore` file, keeping the git status clean after a build. We rely on this to check that we don't have uncommitted changes when releasing generated code from [ocaml-tree-sitter](https://github.com/returntocorp/ocaml-tree-sitter).

~~I also removed the `package-lock.json` file to align with the other tree-sitter-* projects such as https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-javascript/blob/master/.gitignore.~~

/cc @zythosec who started the R integration into semgrep.
